speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of forceful retching followed by sudden chest pain, I suspect a Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture). REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_with_contrast

speaker: Doctor
text: A normal CT scan is unexpected given the classic presentation, so I must consider if the pain is musculoskeletal or referred, or if the initial retching caused a different injury. Do you have any difficulty swallowing or a feeling of food sticking in your chest, and have you noticed any fever or shortness of breath? REQUEST TEST: Esophagogram

speaker: Doctor
text: With a normal CT and esophagogram, I must rule out a Mallory-Weiss tear or severe esophagitis, so I will proceed with direct visualization. REQUEST TEST: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD)

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging and endoscopy ruling out esophageal rupture or tear, I suspect the chest pain is cardiac in nature, possibly triggered by the stress of vomiting. REQUEST TEST: Electrocardiogram (ECG)

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal cardiac and gastrointestinal workups, I suspect the chest pain is musculoskeletal, likely a pectoral muscle strain from the forceful retching. Do you experience increased pain when you move your arms or press on your chest wall? DIAGNOSIS READY: Pectoralis muscle strain secondary to forceful vomiting
